title: He Had Captained Six ODIs Without a Series Win. On Friday, Shubman Gill Scored an Unbeaten 84 to Start Fixing That.
excerpt: India chase down 195 with 13 balls to spare in rain-shortened first ODI against Afghanistan at Dharamsala. Gill crosses 3,000 ODI runs.
body:
Shubman Gill walked into the post-match presentation at the Himachal Pradesh Cricket Association Stadium on Friday evening carrying the weight of a statistic that had followed him for months. Six ODIs as captain. Zero series wins. The critics had been pointed. The questions had been specific. And then, in a rain-shortened 25-over contest against Afghanistan, Gill answered them the only way a batsman can — with his bat.

His unbeaten 84 off 66 balls, laced with 11 fours and two sixes, anchored India's chase of 195 with 13 balls to spare. He was named Player of the Match. More importantly, he crossed 3,000 ODI runs in just 62 innings — joining an exclusive club of Indian batsmen who have reached the milestone before turning 27.

## The Chase That Silenced Doubters

India's pursuit began positively before a mix-up between Gill and Rohit Sharma resulted in the veteran opener's run-out for 16. It was a moment that could have unravelled a young captain. Instead, Gill shifted gears.

With Ishan Kishan — back in the side after losing his central contract and a long spell in domestic cricket — providing explosive support with 34 off 22 balls, Gill built the platform India needed. When Kishan fell to Rashid Khan and Shreyas Iyer departed for 12, the equation still required 49 off the final seven overs.

Enter KL Rahul. The wicketkeeper-batter played one of the most destructive cameos of the Indian summer — an unbeaten 39 off just 19 deliveries, striking four fours and three sixes. Together, Gill and Rahul put on an unbroken 49-run stand that ended the contest with clinical efficiency.

## Gurbaz's Blitz Set the Stage

Earlier, Afghanistan had threatened to post a total well beyond India's reach. Rahmanullah Gurbaz — who went unsold at the IPL auction at a base price of INR 1.5 crore — produced the innings of his career. His 102 off 51 balls, featuring eight fours and eight sixes, was the fastest ODI century for Afghanistan and the second-fastest ever scored against India.

At 142 for three in the 16th over, Afghanistan were cruising. Then Nitish Kumar Reddy yorked Gurbaz, and the collapse began. From 142/3, Afghanistan lost their last seven wickets for just 52 runs.

The debutants did the damage. Gurnoor Brar, the 27-year-old left-arm seamer from Muktsar who once bowled in the nets for the senior team, finished with 3 for 27. Fellow debutant Harsh Dubey claimed 3 for 47. Arshdeep Singh added 2 for 27, while Reddy chipped in with two wickets of his own.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

This was not just another bilateral ODI. It was the first-ever bilateral ODI series between India and Afghanistan — two nations whose cricketing relationship has been defined by ICC events and the IPL rather than home-and-away contests. For the Afghan diaspora in India and the growing number of NRIs who follow both teams, the series represents a new chapter.

It is also a critical audition ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup. With Virat Kohli ruled out with a hamstring injury and Hardik Pandya also unavailable, India are testing their depth. Gill's performance suggests the succession plan is taking shape. At 26, he is the youngest Indian to captain 60-plus ODIs, and Friday's knock was a reminder that his talent is not in question — only the results around it were.

## What's Next

The second ODI will be played at the same venue on Monday, June 16. India lead the series 1-0. For Gill, the job is only half done — a series win would be his first as captain, and a statement that would travel far beyond the Dhauladhar mountains surrounding Dharamsala.

*Sources: ESPNcricinfo, BCCI.tv, CricketAddictor*
